Subject: Executive stability briefing: Acme incident recap + QBR action tracker

Hi team,

Attached is the consolidated postmortem for the 2027-12-08 Acme production degradation (short outage during peak batch window) and an initial action-item tracker intended for QBR review. I pulled together the exec summary so leadership has a single slide's worth of narrative and a clear set of asks for the upcoming QBR:

- Impact summary (TL;DR): 18 minutes of elevated error rates for the hosted text-generation route used by Acme; tail latency spikes caused autoscaling to underprovision during a hot-prefix KV-cache miss pattern. No customer data exposure.
- Root cause: combination of an uncommon tokenization distribution for one partner prompt and a race between cache-population and autoscale policy; our fallback routing didn't trigger because model variant mapping lacked the sequence-length tag.
- Customer impact: Acme saw 4% request failures for critical workflows during their business peak; they flagged escalation to their ops team (cc'd).

Key asks for QBR (owners / ETA in tracker):
1) Short-term: Patch runtime to include sequence-length metadata for variant mapping (owner: Marcus, ETA: 2027-12-15)
2) Mid-term: Autoscale policy adjustment + synthetic load test for hot-prefix patterns (owner: Hannah, ETA: 2028-01-07)
3) Customer communication: Formal incident summary + credit proposal - hand to CS/Sales for sign-off (owner: Vivek, ETA: 2027-12-13)

Attachments: postmortem-redwood-acme-20271208.pdf (4 pages), action-items-qbr-20271212.xlsx (tracker with owners/ETAs), sla-heatmap-dec2027.png (per-route SLA impact visualization).

Please review before Monday's QBR prep sync. Flag anything you think should move into the "blockers" column.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
